items.title: ‘A Private Life’ Review: Jodie Foster Delights (in French!) as a Therapist Who Will Do Anything but Go to Therapy Herself
items.description: Better in asking questions than providing answers, Rebecca Zlotowski’s new film disguises a personal journey as a crime mystery.

items.title: ‘Apocalypse in the Tropics’ Review: Doc on Bolsonaro Era Has Strong Images but Superficial Analysis
items.description: Venice: “The Edge of Democracy” filmmaker Petra Costa takes another hard look at Brazil and the authoritarian forces there vying for power.

items.title: The Loaded Political Legacy of ‘Elite Squad’: How a Brazilian Blockbuster Became a Symbol of the Right-Wing Attitudes it Aimed to Critique
items.description: José Padilha's "Elite Squad" is one of the most iconic Brazilian films of the 21st century, but the badass police epic was far too cool for its own good.

items.title: ‘The Falling Sky’ Review: Documentary Combats Erasure of Native Culture in Amazon Through Filmmaking
items.description: Cannes: Eryk Rocha and Gabriela Carneiro’s Directors' Fortnight entry follows a group of native Yanomami people as they honor the past and try to forge a future.

items.title: ‘Pictures of Ghosts’ Review: Kleber Mendonça Filho Immortalizes Brazilian Cinemas in Deeply Personal Work
items.description: TIFF: The "Bacurau" writer/director turns his camera on the lost movie theaters of Recife in this thoroughly cinematic portrait of film preservation.
